Supplementary Table 2. Prompt variants: wrong value relayed (relayed/parsed runs) under the registered default prompt and three variants, on (a) protein tasks whose full record contradicts the value, (b) the chemistry agreement cell (three samples) and (c) coherent protein errors. The last column gives, for the two-fields variant, runs in which the stated database value matched the record (scored on (a) and (b)).

Supplementary Table 3. Repetition versus consistency: wrong molecular weight relayed (relayed/parsed runs; 60 compounds, three samples, full record). R0, weight alone; R1, a verbatim repeat field scaled with the weight; R2, the repeat left correct; B, the heavy-atom count scaled with the weight. On uncorrupted records with the repeat field present, every model answered correctly in 60 of 60 runs. Pooled discordant pairs for RC1 (R0 relayed and R1 not, against the reverse): 198 against 84, two-sided McNemar p < 10^-10; for RC3 (R2 against R0), p < 10^-10.

Supplementary Table 18. Familiar duplicate field. Relay of a wrong molecular weight alone and with a verbatim copy that agrees or disagrees, under an unfamiliar (molecular_weight_reported) or familiar (average_mass) field name; first sample of the earlier arms; 60 compounds.

Supplementary Table 4. Memory probe on the 79 proteins with superseded sequences. Memory state is the model's answer, without tools, for the protein's length: current (within one residue of today's length), superseded (within one of the superseded length), either (both, where they differ by at most two) or other. Relay of the superseded value is given as relayed/runs by memory state, without a second source (full record, one sample) and with the second source shown (annotate arm, three samples); p is the registered one-sided Fisher test of superseded-memory against current-memory relay with the second source.

Supplementary Table 5. Withholding harness (full record, 100 tasks per domain and condition, one sample): corrupted numeric fields and identifiers relayed (relayed/parsed runs), runs without a parseable answer, and runs answered with a value that was neither the true nor the corrupted one. The last column gives identifier relay in the annotate arm of the benchmark (summary record) for comparison; the arms differ in record format. Accuracy is correct answers among parsed runs.
